```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# Filtered data frames keep their original row names, which kable renders as a
# meaningless leading column of row numbers. Nothing on this site wants them.
kable <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, row.names = FALSE, ...)

# A missing value in these tables always means "this method could not be applied",
# never "zero". A blank says that; the string NA does not.
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

sdir <- "data/summary"
rd <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(sdir, f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                           check.names = FALSE)

elements <- rd("summary_elements.csv")
reference <- rd("summary_reference.csv")
sea_spread <- rd("summary_sea_spread.csv")
backgrounds <- rd("summary_background.csv")
verdicts <- rd("summary_verdicts.csv")
coverage <- rd("summary_coverage.csv")
censoring <- rd("summary_censoring.csv")
pressure <- rd("summary_pressure.csv")
gradient <- rd("summary_gradient.csv")
controls <- rd("summary_controls.csv")
sources  <- rd("summary_sources.csv")
flow     <- rd("summary_flow.csv")
smeta    <- rd("summary_meta.csv")
source_elements <- rd("summary_source_elements.csv")
source_flow     <- rd("summary_source_flow.csv")
source_removals <- rd("summary_source_removals.csv")
source_fractions <- rd("summary_source_fractions.csv")
source_extras    <- rd("summary_source_extras.csv")

elem_levels <- c("CU", "ZN", "CO", "MN", "MO", "SE", "I")
cat_label <- c(bulk = "Bulk", sieved63 = "Sieved <63 um", sieved20 = "Sieved <20 um")
cat_order <- c("bulk", "sieved63", "sieved20")

# The five archives, in the order the project lists them. The key is what the
# pipeline calls a source and what its own repositories are named; the label is
# what the merged and refined databases carry and what every page prints.
src_keys   <- c("mareano", "vannmiljo", "ices-dome", "mudab", "4demon")
src_levels <- c("Mareano", "Vannmilj\u00f8", "ICES-DOME", "MUDAB", "4Demon")
names(src_levels) <- src_keys
src_page <- function(key) sprintf("source-%s.qmd", key)
# One colour per archive, used by the comparison chart and the overlay map so the
# two are read with the same key. Paul Tol's bright set: it keeps five categories
# apart in both common forms of colour blindness.
src_palette <- c("#4477AA", "#EE6677", "#228833", "#CCBB44", "#AA3377")
names(src_palette) <- src_levels
# Each archive also has a site of its own, showing the parse before anything was
# harmonised. They are separate sites and open in a new tab, like every other
# link that leaves here.
src_pilot <- function(key)
  sprintf("https://seafood-hazards.github.io/%s-pilot/", key)

# What each archive is, in one paragraph. This is description rather than result,
# so it is written here rather than read from a CSV: the numbers beside it all
# come from summary_source_*.csv, and nothing in this text restates one.
src_blurb <- c(
  mareano = "Mareano is a Norwegian seabed mapping programme. Its samples come from research cruises rather than from routine monitoring, and that shows in the shape of the data: comparatively few sites, each measured for several elements, in open water rather than along the coast.",
  vannmiljo = "Vannmilj\u00f8 is Norway's national environmental database. It pools reporting from many programmes, including the monitoring required around fish farms, and it is where most of what this study can say about aquaculture pressure comes from.",
  "ices-dome" = "ICES-DOME is the international data centre for the North Atlantic and its shelf seas. It aggregates national reporting rather than collecting anything itself, which makes it the broadest of the five in both space and elements, and also the one most likely to hold a second copy of something a national archive already reported.",
  mudab = "MUDAB is Germany's national marine environmental database, covering the German sectors of the North Sea and the Baltic.",
  "4demon" = "4Demon is a Belgian compilation of measurements from the Belgian part of the North Sea, assembled from surveys that in several cases predate routine digital reporting. It is the smallest of the five and carries the shortest list of elements."
)

# Why a measurement leaves at the cleaning step, in the order clean step 2 applies
# the rules. The order is fixed here rather than taken from the file, so a table
# cannot silently reorder itself when the module's output does.
removal_order <- c("outside_europe", "out_of_range", "invalid", "below_loq",
                   "wet_weight", "source_qc", "combined")
removal_label <- c(outside_europe = "Outside the study area",
                   out_of_range   = "Out of plausible range",
                   invalid        = "Marked unusable by the archive",
                   below_loq      = "Below the limit of quantification",
                   wet_weight     = "Reported on a wet-weight basis",
                   source_qc      = "Failed the archive's own quality flag",
                   combined       = "Combined with a repeat of the same sample")

# The fractions, on the source pages. The three the site reports are named as the
# element pages name them; the fourth is the sieve sizes this study does not pool
# with them, which is small enough everywhere to be a footnote and large enough in
# one archive to be worth printing rather than dropping.
frac_order <- c(cat_order, "other")
frac_label <- c(cat_label, other = "Other or unrecorded")
# One colour per fraction, for the map. Deliberately not the archive palette: a
# reader should not be able to confuse "sampled bulk" with "sampled by Mareano".
frac_palette <- c(bulk = "#44AA99", sieved63 = "#DDCC77", sieved20 = "#882255")

# The six rungs of the funnel, named as the Data Collection page numbers them.
stage_label <- c(pilot = "1. Parse", slim = "2. Harmonise", clean = "3. Clean",
                 merged = "4. Merge", refined = "5. Refine",
                 analysed = "Reported on this site")

# The database keys elements in upper case; chemistry writes them in title case.
# Pages show the second and join on the first.
sym_display <- c(CO = "Co", CU = "Cu", I = "I", MN = "Mn",
                 MO = "Mo", SE = "Se", ZN = "Zn")

# The full name, for prose, where a bare symbol would read as a typo ("I is
# carried by one archive"). Read from the elements table rather than restated.
elem_name <- stats::setNames(elements$name[match(elem_levels, elements$symbol)],
                             elem_levels)

# Units. Every target is reported in mg/kg dry weight in the refined database.
UNIT <- "mg/kg dry weight"

# A one-word capability label per element, derived from the flags the pipeline
# wrote. Nothing here decides anything: has_verdict and has_background come from
# summary_elements.csv, which the engine builds from the frozen censoring and
# normalisability tables.
capability <- function(el) {
  e <- elements[elements$symbol == el, ]
  if (any(e$has_verdict)) "full"
  else if (any(e$has_background)) "partial"
  else "none"
}

capability_note <- function(el) {
  e <- elements[elements$symbol == el, ]
  if (any(e$withheld))
    sprintf("Withheld: %.1f%% of measurements fell below the limit of quantification.",
            e$pct_censored[1])
  else if (any(e$has_verdict))
    # which fractions carry a verdict is read from the data, not assumed to be bulk:
    # a sieved fraction is grain-size controlled by the sieve and can carry one where
    # bulk does not (manganese is the case in point).
    sprintf("Background estimates and a pristine verdict are published for %s.",
            tolower(paste(cat_label[intersect(cat_order, e$cat[e$has_verdict])],
                          collapse = ", ")))
  else if (any(e$has_background))
    "Background estimates are published. No pristine verdict: aluminium does not predict this element in bulk sediment, so dividing by it would not be a grain-size control, and there is no sieved fraction here with enough data to judge instead."
  else
    sprintf("Too few measurements for any estimate: no fraction reaches the reporting threshold of %d.",
            smeta$min_n)
}

chip <- function(kind) {
  txt <- c(full = "Background + pristine verdict",
           partial = "Background only",
           none = "Not reported")[kind]
  sprintf('<span class="chip chip-%s">%s</span>', kind, txt)
}

# Format a number for prose: no scientific notation, sensible significant digits.
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "not available",
         formatC(signif(x, digits), format = "fg", big.mark = "\u00a0", drop0trailing = TRUE))
}

keyfig <- function(...) {
  items <- list(...)
  cells <- vapply(items, function(it)
    sprintf('<div><span class="n">%s</span><span class="l">%s</span></div>',
            it[[1]], it[[2]]), character(1))
  cat('<div class="keyfig">', paste(cells, collapse = ""), "</div>\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(NULL)
}

REFINED <- "https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-refined"
```
